A warm welcome to Clockhouse Primary School
On behalf of the Children, Staff and Governors, welcome to the Clockhouse Primary School Website and welcome to our Clockhouse family. We hope you enjoy the time you spend looking around our site, that you find the information helpful and that it gives you a taste of the happy and industrious school that we are.
Clockhouse is a large Primary School brimming with lots of character. We aim to create a happy and stimulating environment in which pupils are encouraged to develop their character and talents in a supportive community.
Latest News
Weekly reminders for week beginning 28th September 2026
Another good week was had at Clockhouse last week. As always thank you for all you do and your on-going support.
Weekly reminder for week beginning 21st September 2026
Thank you to everyone who helped us remember our much loved member of staff on Friday, I know it meant a lot to us and the family. The children have all settled into the year and we are certainly seeing some fabulous learning taking place across the school. As I walk around the school, it is wonderful to see them so settled, working so hard and showing themselves to 'Be Resilient, Be Consistent, Be Brilliant'. As always, thank you for your on-going support - it really is a team effort in every sense of the word. Thank you to all those who attended Meet the Teacher last week. It was lovely to welcome you. Thank you also to all those parents who are supporting their children and practising the children's reading and spellings with them at home as well as number bond and times tables. Please remember every time the children read at home and you sign their Reading Record book or send a message on Class Dojo, they get a raffle ticket and are entered into our weekly prize draw - you have to be in it to win it!
As always we thank you for your continued support in all we do.
Have a good week everyone!
Weekly reminders for week beginning 14th September 2026
It was certainly lovely to welcome the children from Year 1 to Year 6 back to school this week, as well as welcoming our Reception and Nursery children. The children certainly lived up to expectation and have taken returning to school in their stride. Their adaptability and resilience never ceases to amaze me. They settled so quickly into their classes with lots of learning taking place. We have a VERY exciting week ahead! Meet the Teacher Thank you to all those who came to Meet the Teacher last week. We enjoyed meeting you and hope you found it useful. Meet the Teacher continues this week. Teachers will be in classrooms straight after school and available until 4pm. Please do come and say hello and see your child's classroom. This week is as follows: Tuesday 15th September - Year 5 Wednesday 16th September - Year 2 Thursday 17th September - Greenland (2.45pm) Thursday 17th September - Year 4 Swimming Swimming starts on Monday for Year 4 and Greenland. Year 4 will be swimming every day for the next two weeks so please ensure that they come prepared. Any questions please ask. Wow Day We are very much looking forward to a special event at school on Monday involving the children from Year 2 to 6! Ask them what they got up to when they get home! Exciting Times for Clockhouse We have a number of Headteachers and Senior Leaders from all over the country visiting the school on Tuesday to learn about what we do. We cannot wait to showcase our wonderful school! Year 2 and Year 4 Children in Year 2 and 4 have and exciting VR expeirence coming to school on Wednesday to launch their new topic learning. Please send the money in or pop into the office if you need to pay for this - thank you in advance. Jean's Day Friday will once again be the day where we honour and remember Mrs O'Connor with Jean’s Day. Mrs O'Connor was our former Librarian and Midday Supervision, who suddenly passed away in August 2022. Her favourite colour was purple / lilac so we are asking our Clockhouse family to wear something of this colour in her honour along with non-uniform (PE will continue on this day). Is your child, or a child you know due to start Reception in September 2027 We are looking forward to welcoming prospective parents / carers into school on Thursday 10.00am and 4.00pm. Please call the school to book this or a tour later in the term. Please remember As you know jewellery is not permitted in school. Please ensure children do not come to school wearing this. This includes earrings which should not be worn for school for health and safety reasons. Things to be aware of Following the success of last year, we will be continuing with Achievement Assembly on a Monday to get the week off to a fabulous start. This will be starting on Monday 21st September. The Reading Raffle is back again - when reading with your child at home, please send the teacher a message on Class Dojo or fill in their Reading Diary so that the teacher knows they have read and the children can be awarded with a raffle ticket and entered into the weekly draw. Look out for more exciting news about reading at Clockhouse coming your way soon. Hot Chocolate with the Head continues, children will celebrate with me should they win this award. You will get a call if your child has won to ensure they have permission for this. Please also remember that if children bring things to school, this is done so at your own risk (unless we have directly asked you to do so). We are having a big push on tucking shirts in and taking pride in our appearance. The children are getting very good at this and thank them and you for your support in this. This also includes ensuring the children come to school in the correct PE uniform on PE Days, please help us with this. Letters that went out last week: The following letters went out last week: Nut Free School reminder English Subject Newsletter History Subject Newsletter OCA Newsletter Jean's' Day You Said, We Did VR Experience (Year 2 and 4) Height and Weight Check Information (Reception and Year 6) SATs and Residential Meeting (Year 6) Secondary School applications (Year 6) Walking home (Year 5 and 6) As always we thank you for your continued support in all we do. Have a good week everyone! #ourclockhousefamily Mrs Savidge
Weekly reminders for week beginning 7th September 2026
Welcome back to the new school year everyone! We all hope that you have had and are still having a fantastic Summer Holiday and enjoyed lots of time with family and friends. We are looking forward to hearing about all your adventures and what you have all been up to. As you are aware the staff have already been back to school and have been busy getting the school ready for the children's return. We are very much looking forward to welcoming the children from Year 1 to Year 6 on Monday with Nursery and Reception following in due course. We hope that you are all excited to return. Please do remember that correct School Uniform and PE Uniform should be worn on the appropriate days. A message will be sent on Dojo with regard to PE days. Walking Home (Year 5 to Year 6) Those children in Year 5 to 6 who had permission to leave classrooms on their own last year will be allowed to leave as they did last term for Monday and Tuesday, unless we are told otherwise. A new permission letter will be coming home on Monday for children in Year 5 to Year 6 (as per the letter sent out to some year groups prior to the summer break), the new list will take effect from Wednesday 9th September. Welcome Back Week This week is Welcome Back Week where the children will be concentrating on the basic skills they will need to make this year as successful as possible for them as well as thinking about their learning behaviours and the school values to help them have a successful year. We will also be doing lots of other exciting activities as the children settle into their new year groups. Reception Welcome to our Reception children who have their Stay and Play on Wednesday. We look forward to welcoming the children and their families to Clockhouse and you joining Our Clockhouse Family. Nursery Welcome to our Nursery children who have their Stay and Play on Thursday. We look forward to welcoming the children and their families to Clockhouse and you joining Our Clockhouse Family. Meet the Teacher As many of you know, normally during this time we hold short 'Meet the Teacher' sessions. Dates are on the school calendar but we start this week with Year 6 on Tuesday, Year 3 on Wednesday and Year 1 on Friday. A letter with all dates has already been posted. Class Dojo If you have not yet signed into Class Dojo please ask your class teacher for your login details. If you have a new phone or device and need the password again to access the Dojo please also ask, it really is such a helpful and valuable communication tool for us and you as well as a way of celebrating your children's achievements in school. Following the success of last year, we will only be sending home paper letters in exceptional circumstances and we are sure you do not want to miss anything. Important Dates The calendar on the school website has now been updated with many of the dates for the Autumn Term. Please go to the school website www.clockhouseprimaryschool.co.uk and click on News and Events and then go to the Calendar. Letters that went out last week: The following letters went out last week: Dates for Meet the Teacher and Learn with my Child Things to be aware of: Swimming starts for Year 4 and Greenland on Monday 14th September. Once again welcome back everyone, here is to another OUTSTANDING year at Clockhouse Primary! We cannot wait to see our Clockhouse Family! Have a good week everyone! #ourclockhousefamily Mrs Savidge
Weekly reminders for the week beginning 13th July 2026
And just like that we are in the last week of the term! Where has the year gone. It was lovely to welcome you all into school last week for the different events I hope Early Years and Key Stage 1 enjoyed Sports Day. Thank you to the parents and families who joined us on the last week for the Celebration Assemblies of Brazil and Northern Ireland, we are sure you will agree they were a lovely occasion. We hope you enjoyed reading your child's school report and were proud to read about their year. Please do send the feedback sheets back if you have not done so already. Also may I take this opportunity to thank all those who completed the online questionnaire. Your feedback is certainly very valuable to us! So here we go with the final week... Meet the Teacher The children will be meeting their new teacher on Monday morning and spending time in their new classrooms. We are sure they are all very excited about this - the staff certainly are! Open Evening Do not forget that it is Open Evening after school on Monday (with the exception of the current New Zealand - this is Wednesday), please come into school anytime between 3.30 and 5pm to look at the children's work and meet the teachers. Please also take the time to look around the school and visit your child's new classroom, their current teacher will be able to point you in the right direction. All new teachers will be in school to meet you. Sports Days On Tuesday morning (9.15am) we look forward to welcoming families to the Key Stage 2 Sports Day. Here is hoping the weather is kind to us! It does look like it is going to be hot, please ensure children have hats, water bottles and sun cream applied. Year 2 and 3 Year 2 and 3 will be taking part on a French Storytelling Workshop on Tuesday afternoon. Year 6 Year 6 are very much looking forward to continuing with their Activity Week this week and they have lots of exciting things planned. Please speak to teachers if you have any questions. We are very much looking forward to welcoming the children back to school on Tuesday evening for ClockFest 2026! We look forward to welcoming families to their Leavers Assembly on Thursday at 9.15am - tissues at the ready. Things to be aware of Please remember that school closes for the Summer Holiday on Friday at the normal time. Letters that went out last week: The following letters went out last week: Leavers Lunch (Year 6) Please look out for the July and final newsletter of the year this week. We will be having end of term celebration on Friday with the children! This will also include class parties. This will also be a non-uniform day. Finally from all at Clockhouse we wish you a happy summer holiday and thank you for the support you have given us throughout the year in all we have tried to achieve for the good of the children and the community we serve. You really are OUTSTANDING! We look forward to welcoming Year 1 - Year 6 back to school on Monday 7th September, for an outstanding 2026/2027! Reception and Nursery join us on dates already given. Have a good week everyone and a wonderful holiday when it arrives! #ourclockhousefamily Mrs Savidge

Our Vision, Mission and Motto
Our Mission
Our School – A family and a home for everyone
Our Vision
We are not just a school, we are home!
We lay the foundations for each individual’s future and for dreams to be fulfilled - whatever they may be.
No two bricks are the same but are accepted for their uniqueness and are placed in their own special way to meet their needs.
The cement bonds us together as a family to keep us strong, stable and safe.
We are all safe and happy under one roof, we are protected from the elements and prepared to weather every storm.
The key to success unlocks the door to future achievements unseen before.
The windows show us the reflections of our future self as ready, respectful and responsible adults.
Collaboratively, together our home is decorated with challenge and the rooms are furnished with fun.
All around, a variety of trees grow naturally from the seed of success, with nurture and care anything is possible
So we are not just a school, we are a home that provides a champion for all as well as timeless experiences and skills for a brighter future
And that is why we are called Clockhouse
Ring the bell, we’re always here!

British Values
Teaching British Values
Promoting British Values at Clockhouse Primary School
At Clockhouse Primary School we promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
At Clockhouse these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Democracy:
Democracy is embedded within the life of the school. Pupils have the opportunity to have their voices heard through our School and Class Parliament and Pupil Questionnaires. Our whole school approach to behaviour – the Clockhouse Code is agreed with the children at the beginning of each year.
The Rule of Law:
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that the school abide by are consistently reinforced by all during every school day. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws and rules and with this comes an understanding which is reinforced of the consequences of these being broken.. Visits from pillars of the community such as the Police, Fire Service etc. are part of our curriculum and help to reinforce this message.
Individual Liberty:
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for the children to make safe choices, through the provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advise how to exercise these safely, for example through our Online Safety and PSHE lessons. Our curriculum provides a safe platform from which children can express their views about a range of issues, knowing that these views will be respected and listened to.
Mutual Respect:
Part of our school ethos and approach revolves around kindness and respect for all. This is further reinforced by our three school rules, the ‘Three R’s – ‘Ready, Respectful, Responsible’ An ethos of mutual respect between all aspects of the school community resonates throughout and is developed at any given opportunity.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs:
This is achieved through enhancing pupils understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity. Assemblies and discussions involving prejudices and prejudice-based bullying have been followed and supported by learning in RE and PSHE. The school gives high profile to the range of languages spoken in classes. Members of different faiths or religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school.

Greenland
Welcome to Greenland
Greenland is an exciting place to be, it is part of the continent of North America! Like every Year Group at Clockhouse, we have a fun-filled, creative curriculum to excite and inspire the children of the year group. The adults work hard to ensure that we make the learning in Greenland exciting and memorable. The adults we get to work with are Miss Simmonds, Miss Howlett, Mrs Hodge, Miss King, Mrs Goff, Miss Benson, Miss O’Connor, Miss Rudd, Miss Reed, Mrs Michael, Miss Walshe, Miss Ward and more. We also have a number of other adults who help us learn, make progress and be the best that we can be.
In Greenland, we have three pathways which the children follow depending on their communication needs. These are Explorers, Adventurers and Navigators. The curriculum and approaches are bespoke to meet the needs of the children who access Greenland. This changes with their needs of the children in order to ensure that everyone progresses from their individual starting points. Communication is at the heart of the Greenland curriculum. Our provision is thoughtfully designed to support the development of communication skills, using each child’s preferred method. Through a wide range of opportunities, including play-based learning, we help children build confidence in both expressing themselves and interacting with others.
During the year we will have lots of other exciting events… keep checking the website and letters home for further information.
With so much exciting learning taking place, our pupils thoroughly enjoy their time in Greenland and are always ready to embrace new challenges ahead!

Governors' Report to Parents
Governors' Annual Report to Parents - 2025-2026
The Governing Body is delighted to present its Annual Report to Parents for the 2025/2026 academic year. This report reflects on another highly successful year for Clockhouse Primary School, celebrating the achievements of our pupils, staff and wider school community while outlining the strategic role governors play in supporting the school's continued success.
As governors, our responsibility is to provide strategic leadership, ensure effective financial oversight, hold school leaders to account for educational performance and support the continued development of a school where every child can thrive. We are proud of all that has been achieved this year and remain ambitious for the future.
Clockhouse has enjoyed another exceptional year. Through an unwavering commitment to excellence, innovation and inclusion, the school has continued to strengthen every aspect of its provision. We are particularly proud that Clockhouse remains consistently oversubscribed and continues to be the school of choice for many families within the Collier Row community. This is a testament to the confidence parents place in the high-quality education, exceptional care and extensive opportunities provided for every child.
The quality of teaching and learning remains a significant strength of the school. Staff consistently deliver ambitious, engaging and inclusive lessons that enable pupils to achieve their very best. High expectations, carefully targeted support and a culture of continuous improvement ensure that pupils make excellent progress regardless of their starting points and leave Clockhouse well prepared for the next stage of their education.
This year's assessment outcomes further demonstrate the strength of the school's provision. We are particularly pleased with the achievements of pupils in the Early Years Foundation Stage, the Phonics Screening Check, the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check and the Year 6 statutory assessments. Internal assessment information also demonstrates strong progress across every year group, reflecting both the dedication of our staff and the determination of our pupils.
Reading has remained a central priority throughout the year. The successful completion of the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF) Reading Project has embedded evidence-informed practice across the school and further strengthened our approach to the teaching of reading. Our ongoing partnership with the local Phonics Hub has ensured that staff remain at the forefront of best practice, and we were delighted to receive highly positive feedback following an unannounced phonics monitoring visit. Together, these achievements reinforce our commitment to ensuring that every child develops into a confident, fluent and enthusiastic reader.
Our curriculum remains one of the school's greatest strengths. Designed to meet the needs of all learners, it provides pupils with a rich and engaging educational experience that extends well beyond the classroom. Throughout the year, pupils have benefited from an extensive range of enrichment opportunities, including educational visits, residential experiences, sporting competitions, clubs, themed curriculum days and visitors to school. These experiences broaden horizons, develop cultural capital and create lasting memories that enrich learning.
The Clockhouse curriculum is underpinned by our six curriculum drivers: Aspiration, Challenge, Creativity, Global Citizenship, Cultural Capital and Well-being. These principles shape every aspect of teaching and learning, ensuring pupils leave Clockhouse as confident, resilient and compassionate young people who are well equipped for the future.
Significant investment has also been made in our learning environment. The final phase of our classroom refurbishment programme has now been completed, ensuring every classroom across the school provides a bright and inspiring place to learn. Our Key Stage 1 playground has been transformed with new play equipment and redesigned outdoor spaces, creating exciting opportunities for imaginative play, physical activity and social development. Building upon the success of our Outdoor Play and Learning (OPAL) provision, outdoor learning and play opportunities have also been enhanced within Key Stage 2.
During the autumn term, pupils also enjoyed the unique opportunity of having an on-site swimming pool. This enabled every child to participate in swimming lessons as part of the PE curriculum, ensuring equal access to high-quality swimming instruction and water safety education. This initiative further demonstrated our commitment to providing inclusive and enriching experiences for every pupil.
Inclusion remains at the heart of everything we do. This year saw the introduction of our new Personal Development Team, working under the ethos of Every Child Can. This reflects our belief that every pupil has the potential to succeed and deserves the support needed to achieve their personal best. The appointment of dedicated Pupil Premium Champions has further strengthened our work to reduce barriers to learning and ensure disadvantaged pupils continue to flourish.
Clockhouse is a caring, welcoming and inclusive community where pupils feel safe, respected and valued. Our strong safeguarding culture, positive behaviour ethos and commitment to emotional well-being ensure that every child develops confidence, resilience and a genuine love of learning.
Strong partnerships with parents and carers remain fundamental to the school's success. We are extremely grateful for the trust, encouragement and support shown by our families. By working together, we continue to provide the very best opportunities for every child.
Our values of Nurture, Respect, Learning, Community, Excellence and Excitement remain at the heart of school life. Through our Value Characters and the consistent promotion of these shared values, pupils develop empathy, responsibility, kindness and a strong sense of belonging within the Clockhouse family.
This year also marked an exciting development within our leadership team. We were delighted to welcome our Deputy Headteacher, Mrs Abeledo, who has settled seamlessly into her role and quickly become a highly valued member of the Clockhouse family. Her expertise, enthusiasm and commitment have already made a significant contribution to the continued success of the school.
We are equally proud that our Headteacher's expertise continues to be recognised beyond Clockhouse. This year, Mrs Jo Savidge co-authored the book Outstanding Against the Odds: How Seven Schools Achieve Excellence, alongside Sonia Gill. The publication shares leadership strategies and best practices from schools that have achieved exceptional standards, providing inspiration for educational leaders across the country.
Alongside this achievement, Mrs Savidge has continued to work with other schools through educational consultancy, supporting leaders to strengthen teaching, learning and leadership so that more schools can achieve exceptional outcomes. As governors, we are proud that Clockhouse contributes to the wider educational community by sharing its expertise and supporting school improvement beyond our own setting. This outward-facing approach reflects our belief that successful schools have a responsibility to support others, ultimately benefiting children across the wider education system.
The Governing Body, comprising 12 dedicated governors, has continued to provide effective strategic leadership and robust challenge throughout the year. Governors have monitored progress against the School Improvement Plan and scrutinised pupil achievement, safeguarding, attendance, finance, curriculum developments and the impact of school improvement initiatives. Through regular visits, committee meetings and full governing body meetings, governors have ensured that every decision remains firmly focused on securing the very best outcomes for all pupils. We remain committed to supporting the Headteacher and Senior Leadership Team while fulfilling our responsibility to provide constructive challenge, strategic direction and strong accountability.
This year, we said farewell to Mrs Catherine Neal and Mrs Jo Wright, as they stepped down from the Governing Body. We extend our sincere thanks for their dedicated service, commitment and valuable contribution to the school during their time as governors. We are also delighted to welcome Mr Achillea to the Governing Body and look forward to the knowledge, experience and fresh perspective he will bring to the role.
The Governing Body would like to thank our Headteacher, Deputy Headteacher, Senior Leadership Team and every member of staff for their exceptional dedication, professionalism and passion. We would also like to thank our pupils, parents, carers and the wider community for their continued support. The success of Clockhouse is built upon these strong partnerships and the shared ambition we all have for our children.
As we look ahead to the 2026/2027 academic year, we do so with confidence and optimism. We remain ambitious for every child and committed to continually strengthening every aspect of school life. Through continued investment in our staff, curriculum and learning environment, we are confident that Clockhouse Primary School will continue to provide an exceptional education while remaining a place where every child feels valued, inspired and empowered to succeed.
On behalf of the Governing Body, thank you for your continued support. Together, we will continue to build on the school's many successes and ensure that Clockhouse remains a place where every child is encouraged to achieve, inspired to learn and equipped to flourish.
